methods.label: Find the common ratio first
methods.explanation:
The second and third terms share the factor \(x+1\), so their ratio can reveal the common ratio before we find \(x\).

In a geometric progression, consecutive ratios are defined and equal to the same nonzero number. Hence \(x\ne0\) and \(2x+2\ne0\), so \(x\ne-1\). We may therefore cancel \(x+1\):
\[
r=\frac{3x+3}{2x+2}
=\frac{3(x+1)}{2(x+1)}
=\frac32.
\]
The first two terms must have this ratio as well:
\[
\frac{2x+2}{x}=\frac32.
\]
Multiplying by the nonzero quantity \(2x\) gives \(4x+4=3x\), so \(x=-4\). The first three terms are consequently \(-4,-6,-9\), and both consecutive ratios are indeed \(3/2\). The fourth term is
\[
-9\cdot\frac32=-\frac{27}{2}=-13\frac12.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
